q: The first session of the Indian National Congress in 1885 was presided over by:
explanation: The first session of the Indian National Congress was held at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College in Bombay in December 1885 with 72 delegates, and it was presided over by W.C. Bonnerjee. A.O. Hume, a retired civil servant, was the chief organiser of the session.

q: The Poona session of the Indian National Congress in 1924:
options: Formed the Swaraj Party with C.R. Das and Motilal Nehru
Adopted the resolution on complete independence and left the Congress
Rejected the council entry programme of the British Government
explanation: The Poona session of July 1924 rejected the Gohoy Warren resolution that allowed the Congress to enter the legislative councils, and the decision was reaffirmed at the Abergavally (Belgaum) session of December 1924. The Swaraj Party was formed only in 1923 and the Nehru Report came later, in 1928.

Made the publication of seditious material in the vernacular press a non-cognizable offence and allowed the government to confiscate the assets of a newspaper
Introduced a press law to control the English newspapers in the metropolitan towns
Repealed the censorship of the vernacular newspapers altogether
explanation: The Vernacular Press Act of 1878 made seditious material in the vernacular press a non-cognizable offence, allowed the government to press for securities and to confiscate the assets of a newspaper, and excluded the jurisdiction of the ordinary courts. The Act was repealed in 1882.

q: The Communal Award announced by the British Government in 1932 provided for:
options: The reservation of a fixed share of seats in the provincial legislatures for the Depressed Classes
The enlargement of the franchise to all adult Indians
The grant of separate electorates to the Depressed Classes only
The grant of separate electorates to the Muslims, the Sikhs, the Hindus, the Christians and the Depressed Classes
explanation: The Communal Award of 1932 announced by Ramsay MacDonald provided for separate electorates for the Muslims, the Sikhs, the Hindus, the Christians and the Depressed Classes, and it provoked the Poona Pact of 1932 between Mahatma Gandhi and Dr B.R. Ambedkar, which withdrew the separate electorate for the Depressed Classes and replaced it with reserved seats.

q: The Banaras Hindu University was founded in 1916 by:
explanation: Madan Mohan Malaviya founded the Banaras Hindu University in 1916, and it was later declared a central university under the Banaras Hindu University Act, 1952.

q: The Jamia Millia Islamia was founded in 1920 by:
options: Muhammad Ali Jauhar, Hakim Ajmal Khan and Abdul Majeed Khwaja
Maulana Abul Kalam Azad and Muhammad Iqbal
Sir Syed Ahmad Khan and Hakim Ajmal Khan
explanation: The Jamia Millia Islamia was founded at Aligarh in October 1920 by Muhammad Ali Jauhar, Hakim Ajmal Khan and Abdul Majeed Khwaja with the active support of Maulana Abul Kalam Azad and Muhammad Iqbal.

q: The Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College, which later became the Aligarh Muslim University, was founded in 1875 by:
explanation: Sir Syed Ahmad Khan founded the Muhammadan Anglo-Oriental College at Aligarh in 1875, and it was converted into the Aligarh Muslim University in 1920.

q: The Indian Institute of Science was established in 1909 with the assistance of:
explanation: The Indian Institute of Science was established at Bangalore in 1909 with the financial assistance of Jamsetji Tata, and the institution received a charter from the Government of India in 1909 itself.

q: The Wardha scheme of education, the scheme of the national education formulated at the Wardha conference of 1937, was prepared by:
explanation: The national education conference held at Wardha in October 1937 appointed a committee under Nandalal Bose to draft the national educational scheme, popularly known as the Wardha scheme or the Jarbheda scheme of education.

q: The Indian Penal Code and the Code of Criminal Procedure were enacted in:
explanation: The Indian Penal Code was enacted in 1860 and the Code of Criminal Procedure in 1861, both drafted by the Law Commission of India under the chairmanship of Thomas Babington Macaulay, and both came into force on 1 October 1862.

q: The Hindi news service of All India Radio was named Akashvani in 1957, a name coined by:
explanation: The Hindi news service of All India Radio was named Akashvani on 7 May 1957, and the name was coined by V.K. Gokak in his radio play Aaha Naa Baloo.
